## Analysis of Phased Data

In diploid cells, when a sequenced read overlaps a heterozygous SNP, one is able to group reads according to which chromosome they are sequenced from. Memento can take advantage of this information and can assign changes in methylation states to maternal or paternal chromosomes. __NB:__ without sequencing the parental genomes, one cannot ascertain which parent a chromosome came from - we use the labels maternal and paternal interchangeably.

When phased data is available, each CpG site can be in one of four states: unmethylated on both chromosomes (maternal and paternal (MP): 00), unmethylated on the maternal chromosome and methylated on the paternal chromosome (MP: 01), methylated on the maternal chromosome and unmethylated on the paternal chromosome (MP: 10), or methylated on both chromosomes (MP: 11).

As before, let's load some useful libraries and some simulated data for 100 sites.

```{r load_lib_object}
library(ape)
library(data.table)
library(memento)

data("object_phased")
str(object_phased)
```

And a bit of data cleaning...

```{r clean}
df_meta <- object_phased$meta
filters <- object_phased$filter.param
dt_annotation <- data.table(object_phased$details)
dt_annotation[, chr_pos := paste0(Chrom, "_", Pos)]
setkey(dt_annotation, chr_pos)

tree <- object_phased$tree
tree$tip.label <- gsub("PD40521_Normal_EM1_", "", tree$tip.label)

mtx_list <- object_phased[object_phased$EXTRAFIELDS]

chr_pos_object <- paste0(object_phased$details$Chrom, "_", object_phased$details$Pos)

for(i in 1:length(mtx_list)){
   rownames(mtx_list[[i]]) <- chr_pos_object
   colnames(mtx_list[[i]]) <- tree$tip.label
}

range(tree$edge.length)

tree_di <- tree
if(any(tree$edge.length == 0)){
  tree <- di2multi(tree) # convert to polytomy
}
tree
```

### NB

It is very important for the input data be named and structured correctly when analysing phased data. One must provide a list of matrices with the correct names, which are: `names(mtx_list)`. Here, the part of the string before the underscore, `_`, namely `MT`, `PT` and `U` refer to maternal transcripts, paternal transcripts and unphased, respectively, while the second part of the string, `M` and `U` refer to methylated and unmethylated reads, respectively. Ensure the input data corresponds to this.

Next, we have to update the model to four states.

```{r settings}
settings <- memento_settings()
settings
set_memento_settings(new_number_of_states = 4)
new_settings <- memento_settings()
new_settings
```

Again, let's find changes on the full tree. We start by generating priors and then estimating likelihoods and computing probabilities of assignments in a single step with `compute_probabilities3`.

```{r find_changes_full}
priors_phased <- generate_priors(full_tree = tree, 
                                 m = 2)
# find changes
assignments_phased_full <- compute_probabilities3(priors_per_tree = priors_phased,
                                                 matrix_list = mtx_list,
                                                 n_top_br = 2,
                                                 ro = 0.95, 
                                                 verbose = TRUE)
setkey(assignments_phased_full, Chrom, Pos, rank)
head(assignments_phased_full, 10)

```

Let's plot these results. Since reads are either maternal, paternal or unphased, each CpG site will be plotted as a trio of columns.

```{r hm_full, out.width="700px", out.height="700px", dpi = 300, fig.height=10, fig.width=10, fig.fullwidth=TRUE}
rate_mtx_list <- list("MT_rate" = mtx_list$MT_M/(mtx_list$MT_M + mtx_list$MT_U),
                      "PT_rate" = mtx_list$PT_M/(mtx_list$PT_M + mtx_list$PT_U),
                      "U_rate" = mtx_list$U_M/(mtx_list$U_M + mtx_list$U_U))

assignments_phased_best <- assignments_phased_full[rank == 1,]

some_phased_assignments <- c("n.1:1","58.4:15", "2_33.3:9_10", "27_50.1:3_2",
                             "1_45.3:10_10", "7_32.1:3_3", "1_45.3:9_10")

for(i in 1:length(some_phased_assignments)){
  hm_plot_phased <- plot_heatmap(assignment = some_phased_assignments[i],
                          full_dt = assignments_phased_best,
                          meth_rate_mtx = rate_mtx_list,
                          tree = tree)
  plot(hm_plot_phased)
}

```

## Splitting the Phylogeny

To find multiple independent changes on the full tree, we would have generate many possible expected tip states. To avoid the exponential explosion of plausible tip states, we split the tree into smaller subtrees, assign changes on each of them and then combine the solutions in a recursive manner. For this, Memento relies on an expectation-maximisation approach, where it first uses some *sensible* error rates for gamma and delta to assign changes and then estimates new error rates from thes assignments. This process is repeated until the results stabilise.

```{r four_state_split}
subtrees <- divide_tree_into_subtrees(full_tree = tree, max_subtree_size = 12)
# compute priors
priors_p_subtree_phased <- generate_priors(all_trees = subtrees,
                                           full_tree = tree)
# supply gammma and delta values per site
gv <- rep(0.05, nrow(mtx_list[[1]]))
names(gv) <- rownames(mtx_list[[1]])
dv <- gv

# find changes on each subtree
tryme_phased <- run_EM_on_subtrees(full_tree = tree,
                            subtrees = subtrees,
                            priors_p_subtree = priors_p_subtree_phased,
                            matrix_list = mtx_list,
                            gammas = gv,
                            deltas = dv)

setkey(tryme_phased, Chrom, Pos)
head(tryme_phased, 10)
```

Let's plot the same sites as before.

```{r plot_phased_four, out.width="700px", out.height="700px", dpi = 300, fig.height=10, fig.width=10, fig.fullwidth=TRUE}
earlier_sites_phased <- assignments_phased_full[branch %in% some_phased_assignments,][["chr_pos"]]

tryme_phased_as_before <- tryme_phased[chr_pos %in% earlier_sites_phased,]

same_sites_new_assignment_phased <- names(sort(table(tryme_phased_as_before[["branch"]]), decreasing = TRUE))

for(i in 1:length(same_sites_new_assignment_phased)){
  hm_plot_phased_split <- plot_heatmap(assignment = same_sites_new_assignment_phased[i],
                       full_dt = tryme_phased,
                       meth_rate_mtx = rate_mtx_list,
                       tree = tree)
  plot(hm_plot_phased_split)
}

```
